searchText: I think you are right here, in this case the behavior seems to be equal to the Paris rules (except the error code is different), but the same (old) behavior should work. Maybe <@792822129019584562> could also take a look here? 🙂 Awesome, thanks for taking a look 🙌 this test is included in this PR: https://github.com/ethereum/hive/pull/840 yes we might bot be applying head update because we might be inspecting timestamp in the begining itself for paris/v1 we(ethereumjs) are not validating timestamp as well so v1 will get applied and additional input will just be ignored (most likely) imo the validations whatever can be done in start, should be done in start, so would favor not applying fcU if the timestamp is of future. but ofcourse we should be able to update our validations post applying fcu as well Another slight difference in behavior I just found is that ethJS can reject a payload that has an incorrect BlobGasUsed with `INVALID` even during syncing, which I think makes a lot of sense, geth and nethermind return `SYNCING` I can add a check to accept either of the responses, or force requiring `INVALID` on this specific test case but would like to know the opinion of others <@543900561460822016> <@758579010027782144> IMO the spec does explicitly require this on: > sync is understood as the process of obtaining data required to validate a payload But the information is there because it has the transactions and the blobgasused does not depend on the parent

excerpts.author: jochembrouwer
excerpts.content: I think you are right here, in this case the behavior seems to be equal to the Paris rules (except the error code is different), but the same (old) behavior should work. Maybe <@792822129019584562> could also take a look here? 🙂

excerpts.author: marioevz
excerpts.content: Awesome, thanks for taking a look 🙌  this test is included in this PR: https://github.com/ethereum/hive/pull/840

excerpts.author: g11tech
excerpts.content: yes we might bot be applying head update because we might be inspecting timestamp in the begining itself

excerpts.author: g11tech
excerpts.content: for paris/v1 we(ethereumjs) are not validating timestamp as well so v1 will get applied and additional input will just be ignored (most likely)

excerpts.author: g11tech
excerpts.content: imo the validations whatever can be done in start, should be done in start, so would favor not applying fcU if the timestamp is of future.

excerpts.author: g11tech
excerpts.content: but ofcourse we should be able to update our validations post applying fcu as well

excerpts.author: marioevz
excerpts.content:
Another slight difference in behavior I just found is that ethJS can reject a payload that has an incorrect BlobGasUsed with `INVALID` even during syncing, which I think makes a lot of sense, geth and nethermind return `SYNCING`

I can add a check to accept either of the responses, or force requiring `INVALID` on this specific test case but would like to know the opinion of others <@543900561460822016> <@758579010027782144>

excerpts.author: marioevz
excerpts.content:
IMO the spec does explicitly require this on:
> sync is understood as the process of obtaining data required to validate a payload
But the information is there because it has the transactions and the blobgasused does not depend on the parent
